deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (previous page). Euler builds magic squares whose line sums are 0. Letters with signs are placed so that every row and column cancels, and the diagonal conditions are then imposed. For 3x3 with a 0 in the centre the scheme is [[a+b, -b, -a], [c, 0, -c], [-a-b-c, b, a+c]]. Rows and columns sum to 0 identically. Both diagonals give 2a+b+c=0, so c=-2a-b. The cells are then I a+b, II -b, III -a, IV -2a-b, V 0, VI 2a+b, VII a, VIII b, IX -a-b. The target values are 0, ±1, ±2, ±3, ±4.

THIS PAGE.

(1) 3x3 completion. Setting a=1, b=2 gives [[3,-2,-1],[-4,0,4],[1,2,-3]]. Every row, column and diagonal sums to 0, and the entries are exactly {0,±1,±2,±3,±4}. Adding 5 to each cell gives [[8,3,4],[1,5,9],[6,7,2]]. This is the 'quadratum solitum' (the Lo Shu up to reflection), with magic sum 15.

(2) 4x4 attempt (§VI). The underlying letter scheme is not printed here; it presumably had eight letters a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h with all rows and columns cancelling. The two diagonal conditions are 2a+2b+2e+2f=0 and 2a+2b+2g+2h=0. Hence f=-(a+b+e) and h=-(a+b+g). The resulting cells, row by row, are:
- Row 1: I a+e, II c-e, III -a-b-c-g, IV b+g
- Row 2: V d-e, VI b+e, VII a+g, VIII -a-b-g-d
- Row 3: IX -d+g, X -b-g, XI -a-e, XII a+b+d+e
- Row 4: XIII -a-g, XIV -c+g, XV a+b+c+e, XVI -b-e

XI must be -a-e: Euler's own later list confirms this, and with -a+e row 3 and column 3 would sum to 2e. My reconstruction of the letter forms: XI=f+b, XVI=f+a, X=h+a, XIII=h+b, III=h-c, VIII=h-d, XII=d-f, XV=c-f. The main diagonal I+VI+XI+XVI = 2a+2b+2e+2f and the antidiagonal IV+VII+X+XIII = 2a+2b+2g+2h, as stated. With f and h eliminated, all rows, columns and both diagonals vanish identically in a,b,c,d,e,g.

(3) Pairing idea. The numbers 1..16 minus 17/2 are ±1/2, ..., ±15/2, so the zero-sum 4x4 entries must split into 8 pairs {x,-x} ('socii', i.e. complementary pairs summing to 17). Euler lists the entries whose negatives do not occur: II, III, V, VIII, IX, X, XII, XIV, XV. He then sets g=e to create partners and lists the pairs:
- I a+e / XI -a-e
- II c-e / XIV -c+e
- III -a-b-c-e / XV a+b+c+e
- IV b+e / X -b-e
- V d-e / IX -d+e
- VI b+e / XVI -b-e
- VII a+e / XIII -a-e
- VIII -a-b-d-e / XII a+b+d+e

He observes that some values now occur twice: IV=VI=b+e, VII=I=a+e, X=XVI=-b-e, XIII=XI=-a-e. So 16 distinct numbers are impossible with this specialization, and he concludes the method 'needs a more accurate development'. Source: A. m. T. I p. 28-30.

(4) No. 83 (N. Fuss I, German). A 'light rule' for magic squares of odd order not divisible by 3 that are pandiagonal: the broken diagonals, completed by their opposite parallels, also give the magic sum, and one may start in any cell. The method uses knight steps: each move goes to the next column (one column right, two rows down), wrapping cyclically. If the target cell is occupied, one moves from that blocked cell one column left and two rows down. Checked against the 5x5 example on the next page: 5 is at (4,5), 6 would land on the occupied (1,1), and the rebound gives (3,5), where 6 indeed sits.
errors: X (-b-g) is wrongly included among the entries 'whose negatives do not occur': its negative b+g is IV. Even before setting g=e, IV and X are already socii.
The machine transcription reading XI = -a+e must be -a-e. With -a+e, row 3 and column 3 would sum to 2e, and Euler's own later pairing list has XI = -a-e.
No mathematical error in the 3x3 part. The square obtained is the Lo Shu reflected, which is still magic.
The g=e specialization keeps the square zero-magic but forces the coincidences I=VII, IV=VI, X=XVI, XI=XIII. Euler correctly recognises this ('quidam bis occurrunt') and leaves the problem open.

results.what: 3x3 magic square built as a zero-sum square of letters with centre 0, specialised to values 0,±1..±4 and shifted by 5
results.modern_name: Lo Shu / normal 3x3 magic square via centred (complementary) representation
results.usually_credited_to: ancient (Lo Shu); the centred-value technique is classical (e.g. de la Hire, 1705)

results.what: Parametric description of 4x4 zero-sum magic squares (6 free parameters) and a search for an assignment where entries form ± pairs
results.modern_name: linear parametrisation of the space of 4x4 magic squares; associative/complementary-pair construction
results.usually_credited_to: Frénicle (1693, enumeration of 4x4 squares); linear-algebraic parametrisations later (e.g. 20th century)

results.what: Knight's-move (cyclic step) construction of pandiagonal magic squares of odd order n with gcd(n,6)=1, with rebound rule on collision
results.modern_name: pandiagonal (Nasik/diabolic) magic squares by the knight's-move / de la Loubère-type step method
results.usually_credited_to: de la Hire (1705), with related step methods by de la Loubère (1693)

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragments from the Adversaria printed in the 1862 Opera Postuma and are already known. The 3x3 work is routine. The 4x4 attempt is an abandoned exploratory computation. The knight-move pandiagonal rule is classical and is treated in Euler's published magic-square work (E530, E795).

checkable.sympy: a,b=symbols('a b'); c=-2*a-b; M=Matrix([[a+b,-b,-a],[c,0,-c],[-a-b-c,b,a+c]]); [simplify(sum(M.row(i))) for i in range(3)]+[simplify(sum(M.col(j))) for j in range(3)]+[simplify(M.trace()), simplify(M[0,2]+M[1,1]+M[2,0])]
checkable.asserts: the 3x3 letter scheme with c=-2a-b has all row, column and diagonal sums 0
a=1, b=2 gives the zero-sum square on the page

checkable.sympy: N=Matrix([[8,3,4],[1,5,9],[6,7,2]]); [sum(N.row(i)) for i in range(3)]+[sum(N.col(j)) for j in range(3)]+[N.trace(), N[0,2]+N[1,1]+N[2,0]]
checkable.asserts: the shifted square is magic with sum 15 (all entries 15)

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,d,e,g=symbols('a b c d e g'); Q=Matrix([[a+e,c-e,-a-b-c-g,b+g],[d-e,b+e,a+g,-a-b-g-d],[-d+g,-b-g,-a-e,a+b+d+e],[-a-g,-c+g,a+b+c+e,-b-e]]); [expand(sum(Q.row(i))) for i in range(4)]+[expand(sum(Q.col(j))) for j in range(4)]+[expand(Q.trace()), expand(Q[0,3]+Q[1,2]+Q[2,1]+Q[3,0])]
checkable.asserts: the 4x4 parametric square (with XI=-a-e) has all line sums 0 identically
after g=e, IV=VI, I=VII, X=XVI, XI=XIII (all differences 0): the duplicates Euler notes
IV + X = 0 even before g=e, so X wrongly appears in the unpaired list

transcription_corrections: Row 3 of the 4x4 list: 'XI. -a+e' should read 'XI. -a-e'.
In the pairing list: 'XVI. -b+e' should read 'XVI. -b-e'.
In the pairing list IX is '-d+e' (after g=e); this is consistent with the image.
Arrangement of the pairing list: the left column holds I, II, III, IV / V, VI, VII / VIII and the right column holds their socii XI, XIV, XV, X / IX, XVI, XIII / XII.
